_bio: Lena — Floor 5 (Drone Manufacturing) captive. The street-smart scavenger: a tunnel-runner from the deep levels who came UP through the alien tubes to steal med supplies and got caught above F5. Not staff, not military — the only captive who chose to be in the building. Few words, total loyalty once earned. Knows the tunnels, the club, and codes she shouldn't. Default carrier-candidate for the mole arc (saved-at-Critical). Loyalty arc that opens — late, expensive, on her terms — into a full romance lane: transactional armor cracking, touch as the one thing she never lets herself buy.

nodes.line: *she doesn't scream. She's catching her breath, watching the man on the floor with a scavenger's eyes — checking what he is now the way you check a wire's not live.* ...Huh. *then, to you, hoarse:* Knife. Left ankle. They never check the left ankle.

choices.text: (cut her loose with her own knife)
You're taking this well.
Who are you? You're not staff.

nodes.line: *she's already free of one cuff — there's a bent filament of drone wire in her fingers* Took you long enough. Whole floor heard you coming. *she goes still, reassessing* ...You're not security sweep. You're the noise from downstairs. The one they keep paging about.

choices.text: I'm the noise. Want out?
You almost picked that cuff yourself.

nodes.line: Lena. *that's it. That's the introduction.* I run the deep tubes. Came up for med stock — antibiotics move like currency down there — and a breeder drone tagged me two floors short of home. *she retrieves her knife, checks the edge, sheathes it* Stupid. I knew their sweep pattern changed. Went anyway.

Screaming's spending. *she works her wrists* You scream when someone's close enough to come. Nobody comes to Five. *beat — the look she gives you is the closest she gets to surprise* Almost nobody. Lena. I run the deep tubes.

Staff. *the word comes out like spoiled food* No. Staff is who I steal from. Lena. Tunnel-runner. There's a whole world under this building's basement, and I'm the best courier in it. Or was, before the drone.

Almost. *she flexes the wire and flicks it away* Drone filament. Good for cuffs, bad for the strap rig they were about to move me to. So your timing's the only reason I'm being polite. Lena. Deep-tube runner. You want the toll-free version of this building? Stick with me.
Trade. You got me off the rig, so you get one answer free. After that, everything costs — that's tunnel law. *she waits. The question IS the test.*

choices.text: What's under this building?
How do I get to Floor 7 fast?
Are you okay? That's my question.

nodes.line: *a slow blink — right question* Everything. Tubes, big as freeway bores, smooth like something MELTED them. Old. Older than the lab — the lab plugged INTO them, not the other way around. There's caves with singing rock, a flooded level, and at the very bottom there's a door with a number on it and music behind it. *she shrugs* I don't ask the bottom questions. Bottom questions cost the most.

Elevator's watched, stairs are gassed past Six. But the freight shaft behind the recharge depot runs express if you know which panel lies. *she taps her temple* I know every panel that lies in this building. That's answer one. Going UP with you costs nothing — I'm headed that way regardless. Out is up. Out is always up.

*long pause. The question costs HER something to answer, which makes it expensive, which means you spent your free one on her.* ...No. *she says it plainly, once, and puts it away* But I will be. Down-tunnel we don't waste breath on the gap between those two. *she squares her pack straps* You spent your free question on a runner you just met. That buys you more than you know.
Deal stands: you're the gun, I'm the map. Don't slow down for me. I was born not slowing down.

pool.line: Camera. *she's pointing before you see it* Eleven o'clock, dead lens. Somebody shot it out years ago. Friend of mine, probably.
Vents in this place run warm-cold-warm. The cold runs go DOWN. File that.
Static says hello, by the way. You'll meet her if you ever find the bottom door. Tell her I'm holding my own marker.
You went back for the club door, huh. Knew you were a bottom-questions type the day you spent your free one on me.
The cells on One have terminals. Old ones. Some of those rooms had locks on the INSIDE once. Think about what that means.
*she watches a surveillance drone drift past without targeting you* ...They drift wrong lately. Like they're listening to something further down. *she doesn't elaborate. She doesn't know how to.*
I had a brother. Tunnel took him — flood level, bad map. It's why my maps are good, Jake. Every line on them is paid for.
Most people I guide, I'm counting what they're worth if they don't make it. Stopped counting you somewhere around Floor Three. Don't make me start again.
*she passes you in the corridor and palms something into your hand: nothing. An empty palm. Just the touch.* Toll. Pay it. *she's gone, almost smiling*
Found a room on Three with a door that actually locks. *she says it like trade intel. It is not trade intel.*
Down-tunnel you share heat to survive. Up here apparently you share it because it's GOOD. Still adjusting. Keep helping.
Stopped pricing your hands. *beat* Started pricing every hour they're not on me. Expensive day so far.
Drew a route last night. Shortest path between us. *flat* It's zero, Jake. The route is zero. Stand closer.
Marco's tags don't get cold anymore. Sleep next to a furnace, that's why. *the furnace is you. She will not be saying more words about it.*

sidequest._hook: THE CACHE — her stash sits in the F1 under-hall (the hidden yellow route, HIDDEN_AREAS_AND_BIOMESH.md): meds, a dead friend's tags, and a hand-drawn tunnel map. Leads the player to the under-hall / bookshelf-elevator architecture and seeds the 1278 terminal-code discovery. Reward: the tunnel map item + the under-route revealed.

nodes.line: Toll-free tip, one time only, because you keep not dying: I've got a cache under Floor One. Under-hall — there's a hall under the hall; staff never knew, that's the POINT. Antibiotics, a charge cell, and... personal stock. Drone tagged me before I could clear it. *beat* I'd rather it feeds us than feeds dust. And I'd rather you saw the under-hall from me than found it the hard way. Some of those doors only pretend to be furniture.

choices.text: Show me the hall under the hall.
Personal stock?
Doors that pretend to be furniture?

nodes.line: Armory's got a floor that lies. Stair under it. Three ways out of that under-hall, and only one of them was built by the people who think they own this building. *she's already plotting the route on the back of a ration wrapper* Move quiet on the stairs. The monitoring post up top is glass — they see motion, not faces. Faces cost extra.

*flat* Tags. Marco's. My brother — the flood level kept him, but I dove for the tags. They live in the cache because carrying them up here felt like bringing him somewhere worse. *she looks at you, daring you to make it soft* Now you know what's in the box. Help me get the box.

Bookshelf on the under-route. Looks like staff clutter. It's a box that goes DOWN — one room, one cable, old as the tubes. I never rode it; it wants a signal I don't carry. *she taps her own forearm, unconsciously* Something under the skin. The barricaded ones in the bio-lab might know. They built half that floor's lies.

nodes._trigger: fired when the cache is recovered in the under-hall
nodes.line: *she splits the meds without being asked — half to Aria's kit if Aria lives, half to her pack. The tags she holds for one breath, then loops over her neck, done deciding.* Marco rides along. He'd have liked you — you don't slow down. *she hands you the cloth map, the real treasure: every tube, every liar panel, every depth marked in her tight little hand* Map's yours. I'm your map now anyway. That's the whole cache, Jake. That's everything I own. *beat* Worth more than what it cost. First time I've ever said that.

trust._scene: Rel 2 + mercy axis >= 55 (she watches how you treat the helpless ones — surrendering guards, panicked scientists; that's HER axis). The code scene: she pays her debt in the only currency she has.

nodes.line: Settle up time. Tunnel law: debts compound, and I don't like owing. So here's the most expensive thing I carry. *she crouches, draws four digits in the dust, then wipes them with her palm almost immediately* One-two-seven-eight. There's a terminal in one of the old cells on Detention that takes it. I watched a man come OUT of the floor of a locked cell once, Jake. Out of the FLOOR. He walked to the elevator like he owned the dark, and he was never on any roster I ever traded for.

choices.text: Who was he?
Why give me this now?
(just memorize it) Twelve seventy-eight.

nodes.line: Bottom question. *but she answers it, which tells you what you've become to her* Down-tunnel they call him the Architect. Built things before the lab was the lab. Static says he built the bottom door too — the one with the music. I say nobody builds a nightclub at the bottom of the world unless they're planning to stay. *she stands* That's all I know and half of what I guess. Spend it well.

Because you keep choosing the expensive thing. The guards that quit — you let them quit. The lab coats under the desks — you stepped past. Down-tunnel we count that. *she shrugs, embarrassed by her own arithmetic* Ledger says you're good for it. Ledger's never wrong. People are wrong. Ledgers, no.
*a short nod — the right amount of words, which is none* ...Yeah. You'd have made a runner. *it is, from her, approximately a medal of honor*

romance._scene: Opt-in declaration, declinable at zero cost. Gate: rel 3 + love >= 70. Tunnel law has no word for wanting without owing — she asks Jake to supply it. Heat 3/5 here; the burn comes later.

nodes.line: *she's been quiet a full day — even for her. Then, at the night hold, she sits down across from you, knees almost touching, and lays her knife on the floor between you like an opening bid* Settle-up problem. *she frowns at her own hands* Tunnel law says everything costs and every debt clears. But the ledger's clean, Jake. You don't owe me. I don't owe you. And I still — *the next words cost her more than the code did* — I still want my hands on you. Want yours on me. No trade attached. There's no WORD for that down-tunnel. *she looks up: dark eyes, steady, terrified, certain* So you say it. Whatever it's called up here. Say it and it's yours.

choices.text: It's called being mine, Lena. Free. No tolls, ever.
(move the knife aside and take her hands)
Lena — I can't take this. The route stays as it is.

nodes.line: Mine. *she tries the word like testing a rope — full weight, slowly* ...Doesn't cost anything. Just sits there. Being true. *the smallest, realest smile you will ever see in this building* Stupidest economics I ever heard. *she moves around the knife and fits herself under your arm — deliberate, decided, done* Okay. New map. No tolls anywhere on it. Don't slow down for me. *beat* Slow down for me sometimes.

*her hands close around yours, hard — a runner catching a thrown line* ...Yeah. *that's it. That's the whole speech. But she doesn't let go for an hour, and Lena has never once in her life held anything she wasn't ready to drop.*

*she nods once, picks up the knife, sheathes it — no wound anywhere in the motion; she priced this branch before she sat down* Clean ledger's still the best thing I own. *she settles against the wall beside you, same as every other night, loyal as gravity* Route stays. Best one I ever ran. Nothing's lost, Jake. Down-tunnel, a night where nothing's lost is a RICH night.

desire._scene: Slow-burn escalation (heat 4/5). Twelve years of never-touching, spending itself. Gate: lena.romance. Decline costs nothing; her offer has no expiry.

nodes.line: *resupply stop. She's rewrapping her knife grip — and then she isn't. She's watching your hands strip the rifle, openly, the way she watches nothing, because watching is information given away free* ...Problem. *she sets the knife down* I keep catching myself staring at your hands. Trying to price them. Can't. Only thing in this building I can't put a number on. *she stands, crosses to you, and lays one finger on your wrist — barely a touch; from Lena it's a confession at full volume* Down-tunnel you don't touch what you can't pay for. *her eyes come up* Tell me they're not for sale. Tell me they're already mine and I'll stop rationing.

choices.text: (turn your hand over, lace her fingers through) Already yours. Stop rationing.
Take what's yours, runner.
Not tonight, Lena.

nodes.line: *her breath goes out of her like a held door released. Then her hands move — over your knuckles, up your forearms, slow and starved, twelve years of never-touching spending itself all at once* Warm. *she sounds almost angry about it* You're WARM. Nobody told me you get to just... HAVE this. *she presses her forehead to your sternum, fingers fisted in your shirt* Find us somewhere with a door, Jake. I want one night where I hold something and nobody takes it.

*the look she gives you could strip a wire* Careful. Runners take EVERYTHING that's theirs. *she steps in — quick, certain, a route committed to — and kisses you once, hard, teeth and intent, then steps back with your jacket zip somehow already down, grinning like a successful theft* Down payment. The rest wants a locked door and a long night. *over her shoulder* I've already scouted three.

*the finger withdraws, unbothered — a runner reads a closed route and reroutes, no drama* Copy. *she goes back to the knife wrap. Then, not looking up, with almost a smile:* Offer stands. No expiry. First thing I ever put on the table without a clock on it.

night._scene: Private culmination (heat 5/5). Gate: rel 3+, lena.romance, lena.desire, host-set loc.private. She sets rules, then abandons them; decline costs nothing and re-offers.

nodes.line: *the safe room. She checks which panel of the door lies — habit — then bolts it and stands a second with her back to you. When she turns around, the armor's already on the floor with her pack; what's left is just Lena: slight, scarred, braver than the whole building* Rules. *she crosses to you and stops close* One: I have never done this without counting what it cost. Two: I'm not counting tonight. Three — *her hands flatten on your chest; her voice drops to almost nothing* — if I forget how to stop holding on, you don't tell anyone. Runner's reputation. *she looks up* Last chance to reroute, Jake. After this, you're load-bearing.

choices.text: Hold on, Lena. I'm not going anywhere.
(tilt her chin up and kiss her — slow, no clock on it)
Tonight we just hold the room. Sleep next to me.

nodes.line: *she comes apart quiet — of course she does; screaming's spending — but the silence she gives you is louder than anything in the building: her breath catching at every new place your hands learn, her fingers mapping your shoulders like terrain she is claiming for good, her body pulling you in with a strength that's all wiry tunnel-grace and zero apology. She holds on. She forgets how to stop. And somewhere deep in the night she says your name against your throat — once, paid in full, the most expensive word she owns — and after that, nothing in the room costs anything at all.*

*after. She's wrapped around you completely — arms, legs, total commitment, a runner's grip on a lifeline — cheek over your heart, one finger moving slow across your back. You realize she's drawing: corridors, junctions, a route.* ...Map of you. *drowsy, unashamed* Best terrain I ever charted. No tolls anywhere on it. The Architect never built anything this good. *her grip tightens once, on purpose: keeping* Marco would laugh himself sick. His sister. Holding on. *and then, barely audible, the entire treasury:* Worth more than what it cost. You. Always.

*a single nod — she banks it like supplies. Then she surprises you anyway: drags her bedroll flush against yours, first time ever* Holding the room. Together. *she settles with her back against your chest and pulls your arm over her like a strap she chose herself* ...This part's free too, huh. *a long exhale — ten years of watchfulness going off-shift at once* Tunnels never had this.

afterglow._scene: Morning after (warm, character-deepening). Gate: lena.night, plays once. Runners leave before light. She stays.

nodes.line: *first light, or what passes for it down here. Runners leave before light — every story she's ever told you says so. Lena is still there. Awake, chin on your chest, watching you, and she has clearly been there a while* Stayed. *she announces it like a finding from an expedition* Whole night. Didn't check the exits once. *she crawls up and kisses you — unhurried, luxurious, a woman spending from a full account* New rule, and this one's free: the route runs two-way now. You get lost, I come find you. I get lost — *the pause IS the trust* — you come find me. Deal's done. No takebacks. I already drew you on the map.

choices.text: Deal. Two-way. Forever.
You drew me on the map?

nodes.line: Forever. *she taps the word against your sternum like testing rock — solid — then rolls out of the bunk, all business again. But she leaves her knife lying next to your gear while she washes up. Lena. Leaves her knife. Inside someone else's reach. Down-tunnel, that's the whole wedding.*

*she produces the cloth map. There, by the under-hall, in her tight little hand: a new marker. A small star, and one word — HOME. She watches you read it, chin up, daring you to make it soft.* Cartography's honest or it's useless. *beat* Don't slow down. *quieter* ...Slow down a little.

carrier_confront._scene: THE MOLE ARC (player-discoverable; see STORYLINE_EXPANSIONS c). Gate: lena.carrier (set silently if she was rescued at InfectionStage::Critical) + the player has seen 2+ breadcrumb events (drones not targeting her, a door she shouldn't know, sleep-talking in a flat second voice). Triggered by the PLAYER choosing to confront. She does not know.

nodes.line: *you lay it out: the drones, the door codes, the voice in her sleep. She listens the way she checks a wire — utterly still. Then she pulls her knife, reverses it, and offers you the grip.* Then there's something in me that didn't get interrupted. *her voice doesn't shake. That costs her everything you can't see.* I told you screaming's spending, Jake. So I'm not going to scream. I'm going to ask you what the map says we do, because I can't read this one. First map I can't read.

choices.text: We cure it. Whatever it takes — the synthesis lab, the Salvari, all of it.
You stay with us. Watched. We use what it hears against them.
(take the knife) You know what you'd do in my place.

nodes.line: *she looks at the refused knife for a long moment, then sheathes it* ...Cure. *the word comes out foreign — she's never once budgeted for rescue, only for exits* Okay. New map. *quieter, the only crack she allows:* Marco would say I finally guided somebody worth the toll. Don't prove him wrong, Jake. I just put everything I own on you. Again.

A tapped wire. *she turns the idea over; tunnel pragmatism wins over fear, barely* Runners carry packages without reading them all the time. Fine. I carry this one BACK at them. *she sets her own conditions, flat and absolute:* You watch me when I sleep. Aria checks me at every hold. And if my hands ever start a map I don't remember drawing — *she taps the knife* — the toll's already agreed. Say it back to me so I know you heard.

*she doesn't flinch. She closes your fingers around the grip properly — a professional correcting an amateur's hold, one last lesson.* Edge out. Wrist firm. *and then, the only time she ever says this many words this softly:* Down-tunnel we don't waste breath on goodbyes either. You were the best route I ever ran, Jake. Make it clean and make it COUNT — both or neither. *what you do next is on you. The game should make you live with either.*

infected_lost._use: If Lena is never saved / the carrier strand completes untreated.

nodes.line: *the voice is hers but the economy is gone — it spends words like they're free now, and that's how you know* Jake. Jake, Jake. The maps were always wrong, did you know? Every tunnel I ever ran was a vein. We weren't moving THROUGH something, we were moving INSIDE something. And it's awake now, and it knows every route I know. *a smile she never wore* No tolls anymore. Everything's free down here. Come down. Come DOWN.
